title: api-gateway: routing tweaks and streaming proxy buffer/payload limits for stability and OpenAI compatibility
author: Alex Chen
description:
Motivation: Recent customer incidents and internal perf canaries surfaced two classes of failures at the API gateway: (1) routing decisions under high fanout sometimes routed streaming requests to cold/backpressure-prone backends causing stall/retries, and (2) the streaming proxy's buffer sizing and per-request payload limits led to dropped partial function-call tokens and truncated structured output when routing through the OpenAI-compat layer. This PR performs coordinated changes across the API gateway routing policy, streaming proxy, and OpenAI compatibility layer to improve streaming stability and preserve structured/function-calling semantics under backpressure.

Summary of changes: 1) Introduce weighted routing policy that factors backend capacity and recent tail-latency (short sliding window) and prefer local cached KV-serving nodes for continuation-heavy streams. 2) Increase streaming-proxy in-memory buffer to 5MB per-connection (configurable) with adaptive flush thresholds to avoid head-of-line stalls. 3) Expand per-request payload limit for streaming+function-calls from 1MB to 4MB when the route is explicitly tagged as streaming-heavy; routes still enforce a hard upstream limit to protect legacy backends. 4) Adjust OpenAI-compat streaming parser to avoid splitting function call JSON tokens across chunks; add a small reassembly buffer and an "incomplete_token" framing marker. 5) Add metrics, tracing tags, and an alert rule for repeated reassembly events and route-ejection counts. 6) Add end-to-end integration test that simulates backpressure and verifies function-call delivery and structured output integrity across the gateway and compat proxy.

Checklist:
- [x] Routing policy impl + unit tests
- [x] Streaming proxy buffer changes + benchmarks
- [x] OpenAI-compat reassembly logic + integration tests
- [x] Updated defaults and config flags with sensible fallbacks
- [x] Docs + upgrade notes for Dedicated/Private operators

Rationale and compatibility notes: The default behavior remains conservative (1MB payload limit and 2MB buffer) unless operators opt into the streaming-heavy route tag or autoscaler detects a sustained continuation workload, so this is not a silent breaking change. The OpenAI-compat reassembly is backwards compatible: frames that already contain final tokens are passed through unchanged; only incomplete JSON tokens are buffered and flagged. Rolling deploys are safe because routing will prefer healthy nodes and the increased buffer is per-proxy so memory impact is bounded and configurable.

Related linear items: ENG-4821 (streaming stability), ENG-5010 (openai-compat fixes). Related PRs: pr-21534-api-gateway-routing-and-streaming-stability, pr-28142-api-gateway-routing-payload-streaming-buffers.

review_thread: Priya Raman: Can the weighted routing policy be tuned at runtime? Concerned about rollout safety on multi-tenant nodes.
Alex Chen (author): Yes — weights and window size are exposed via config and hot-reloadable. Added docs and a default conservative window.
Diego Martinez: Buffer increase looks fine but please add an operator tunable to limit per-proxy memory under high concurrency.
Alex Chen (author): Added per-proxy global cap and per-connection max. Updated config defaults to 5MB/connection and 1GB/proxy cap.
Samir Patel: OpenAI-compat reassembly seems correct but add a test that reproduces a real-world function-call chunking pattern (split inside a string escape).
Alex Chen (author): Added integ test that specifically splits inside JSON string escape sequences and asserts correct reassembly and function-call invocation delivery.
release_notes: Improvements: API Gateway routing now factors backend capacity and tail-latency for streaming requests; streaming proxy buffer and per-request payload limits increased for streaming-heavy routes (configurable). Fixes: OpenAI compatibility streaming parser will no longer drop or split function-call JSON tokens across chunks. Operator impact: operators may opt into higher per-request limits for streaming routes; default behavior unchanged.
notes_for_release_engineering: Coordinate canary rollout to Dedicated zones first and monitor metric 'gateway.streaming.reassembly.count' and 'gateway.route.ejections' for spikes. Default values preserved; if operators run on low-memory nodes, consider keeping legacy limits.
